prompt: Read-only architecture consult. Pocket Spatial is a working iPhone 6 / iOS 12.5 Safari Web Audio spatializer. We have now added a SoundCloud OAuth connector that intentionally exposes only the authenticated user's own uploads. The remaining problem is playback transport: for one own upload, SoundCloud's authenticated /tracks/{track_urn}/streams returns AAC-HLS URLs, but Safari 12 historically does not reliably expose HLS media-element PCM through MediaElementAudioSourceNode for Web Audio processing. We must not proxy or capture arbitrary third-party tracks. Because these are the authenticated user's own uploads, assess the fastest technically honest way to get such a track into the existing browser spatial DSP on iPhone 6. Compare: (A) try native Safari HLS <audio> -> MediaElementAudioSourceNode and feature-test whether PCM actually flows; (B) Worker resolves authenticated SoundCloud stream to a signed CDN URL and browser feeds that <audio> source to Web Audio; (C) browser fetches HLS playlist/segments and decodes AAC using only APIs available in iOS 12 Safari; (D) abandon web transport for SoundCloud playback and add a minimal iOS 12 UIKit/AVFoundation/AVAudioEngine native app while retaining the web player for local files. Do not propose server-side transcoding/relaying unless there is no compliant alternative, and state legal/API caveats clearly. Do not modify repo files.
context: Existing Web Audio graph is ES5 and uses only MediaElementAudioSourceNode, ChannelSplitter, DelayNode, BiquadFilterNode, GainNode and ChannelMerger. It is tested on a mocked graph but not yet physically tested on Alex's iPhone 6.
Current SoundCloud connector keeps client secret and real OAuth tokens in a Cloudflare Worker. The page has only an opaque encrypted session token.
Current SoundCloud scope is /me and /me/tracks only; every listed track is marked own_upload and linked back to SoundCloud.
SoundCloud current stream endpoint is authenticated and modern stream family is AAC HLS, typically 160k then 96k fallback.
Target is something Alex can actually hear on an iPhone 6, not a theoretical browser demo. Stability and truthful capability detection matter more than elegance.
expected_response: Under 1000 words: decisive recommendation; exact first experiment; how to feature-test success/failure on iOS 12; whether signed-CDN pre-resolution helps; what absolutely cannot work in Safari 12; native fallback architecture if browser fails; and the next implementation sequence. Be conservative about claims and distinguish facts from things requiring device verification.
